claims.claim: Didymus the Blind was born c. 313 in Alexandria, Egypt and died c. 398 in Alexandria.
Didymus the Blind headed the influential catechetical school of Alexandria.
Didymus the Blind was blind since childhood and remained a layman all his life.
Athanasius the Great, bishop of Alexandria, made Didymus head of the Alexandrian school.
Didymus was a leading opponent of Arianism.
Didymus was a faithful follower of Origen and adopted many of his views.
The works of Didymus, but not his person, were condemned by the Second Council of Constantinople in 553 for teaching the doctrine of Origen.
Because of this condemnation, most of Didymus's works were not copied during the European Middle Ages and thus were lost.
Didymus taught for about half a century in Alexandria.
Many of Didymus's writings are lost, but some of his commentaries and essays survive.
